sources.name: gnomAD v4.1 (exomes and genomes) allele frequencies

version.value: v4.1 (4.1.2 for constraint); site shows v4.1.2, v3.1.2, v2.1.1

sources.scope: 730,947 exomes and 76,215 genomes mapped to GRCh38 (v4); site-level allele counts per ancestry group, group-maximum and filtering allele frequencies, and in-silico scores carried in INFO (CADD, REVEL, SpliceAI, Pangolin, PhyloP, SIFT, PolyPhen) plus GA4GH VRS allele IDs. The header of the exome file defines 413 INFO fields and that of the genome file 240. The joint callset (exomes and genomes pooled, 664 INFO fields) carries joint, exome and genome counts side by side and the filters BOTH_FILTERED, EXOMES_FILTERED, GENOMES_FILTERED and PASS; it holds no predictor scores.
sources.mapping_methods: Coordinates on GRCh38 (v4, v3) or GRCh37 (v2.1.1 with liftover files).

quantitative.summary: Allele counts (AC), numbers (AN), frequencies (AF), homozygote counts, group-maximum (grpmax) and filtering allele frequencies (faf95/faf99) per site and per ancestry group; predictor scores per allele.
quantitative.units: counts / frequency in [0, 1]; CADD phred; the other predictors on their own [0, 1] or signed scales
quantitative.uncertainty: AC/AN; filtering allele frequencies give a conservative lower bound; no confidence interval on AF
quantitative.direction: n/a (predictor scores point towards deleteriousness as defined by each tool)

licence.name: Primary exome/genome data released under CC0; some annotations carry separate terms (SpliceAI is CC BY-NC 4.0)
licence.redistribution: CC0 for primary data; honour separate annotation terms

sources.update_frequency: Major releases every few years; point releases (4.1.1, 4.1.2) in between.
coverage_limitations: An allele missing from a slice was not observed in the callset or was removed by QC; it is not a measured frequency of zero, and coverage tracks are not fetched
Case-control/cohort composition affects representativeness
Not a random sample of any population
Per-chromosome VCFs are very large (e.g. exome chr1 17.56 GiB, genome chr1 41.25 GiB)
The regional slices kept here cover only the positions of MaveDB-mapped SNVs (about 146k positions in about 1.5k regions); other regions must be sliced the same way when needed
known_omissions: Individual-level genotypes not available
Allele-frequency filtering bias against disease cohorts is noted by the consortium

reuse_decision.rationale: Whole-chromosome VCFs (11-67 GiB each) are not mirrored. The files are bgzip + tabix on a public bucket, so regions are read by HTTP range requests: slices for the genomic positions that our assets name (MaveDB-mapped SNVs) are fetched and kept; the same primitive serves later lookups for variants of interest. Absence of a record in a slice means not observed or filtered out, not a frequency of zero.

status.notes: Remote tabix over the proxy works (index opens in about 1 s; a region read takes about 0.5 s). Slices for the MaveDB positions are written by acquisition/fetch_gnomad_regional.py.

Post-mortem tissue; some tissues have few samples
Only open-access data are available here

sources.name: MaveDB (Multiplexed Assays of Variant Effect database)

version.value: API 2026.3.2; bulk dump v4 (Zenodo 20840937)

sources.scope: Published MAVE score sets (deep mutational scanning, MPRA and related assays). The public search lists 2,938 published score sets; 1,402 have a human target (1,320 by organism filter + 82 by GRCh38/transcript accession).
sources.mapping_methods: Per-score-set target sequence or accession; MaveDB maps variants to genomic coordinates in a separate step (mapping state complete for 888 of 1,402 human sets in our records). Ensembl distributes a coordinate-mapped TSV for VEP.

quantitative.summary: Assay-specific scores with optional sd/se/other columns; 91 of the 1,320 organism-filter sets carry score calibrations.
quantitative.uncertainty: sd/se columns in many sets; absent in others
quantitative.direction: defined per score set; must be read from its metadata

licence.name: Per record: CC0 (1,340), CC BY 4.0 (45), CC BY-SA 4.0 (11), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (6) among our 1,402 human sets; Zenodo bulk dump contains CC0 records only
licence.redistribution: Follow each record licence; private repository status does not override it
licence.note: Counts from our API-built records; Zenodo licence from the record metadata (cc-zero).

sources.update_frequency: Continuous; Zenodo bulk dumps on versions dated 2024-05-20, 2024-11-15, 2025-06-12, 2026-02-06 and 2026-06-25.
coverage_limitations: Uneven gene coverage; most sets are missense/small-variant libraries of one gene or domain
Scores are not comparable across score sets without per-set calibration
Mapping to genomic coordinates incomplete (888 complete, 321 incomplete, 181 failed, 9 queued of 1,402)
322 of 1,402 sets have processing state incomplete
known_omissions: Private/unpublished score sets
Variants not assayed; absence of a score is not evidence of no effect

reuse_decision.rationale: Metadata and 1,980 score/count tables are already downloaded and verified (scrape/mavedb-human, data/mavedb-scores). The Ensembl coordinate-mapped file and the Zenodo v4 dump are being compared against it before any change.

status.notes: API open; Zenodo reachable with an identifying user agent (generic curl user agent was refused earlier).

sources.name: Open Targets Platform
sources.scope: Integrated target-disease evidence. The 26.09 output has 61 datasets, including: credible_set, study, variant, colocalisation, l2g_prediction, enhancer_to_gene, baseline_expression, interaction, target_essentiality (DepMap), evidence_crispr/evidence_crispr_screen, evidence_impc, evidence_clingen, evidence_eva (ClinVar), evidence_gwas_credible_sets, evidence_gene_burden, evidence_genomics_england, evidence_uniprot_variants, pharmacogenomics, mouse_phenotype and reactome. The variant dataset states that all variation is mapped to GRCh38 with 1-based gnomAD-style identifiers (chrom_pos_ref_alt) and population allele frequencies from gnomAD 4.1.
sources.mapping_methods: Evidence is mapped to Ensembl targets and EFO diseases by Open Targets pipelines; variant-level datasets keyed by GRCh38 coordinates (assembly not confirmed from the live evidence).

quantitative.summary: Association scores, credible-set posterior probabilities, colocalisation statistics, locus-to-gene scores, essentiality scores.
quantitative.uncertainty: credible-set PIPs and coloc posteriors where provided

licence.name: CC0 1.0 for Platform data (docs page); a separate data-source licensing list exists on the same page
licence.redistribution: CC0 for the Platform; upstream source terms should be checked from the data-source list

coverage_limitations: Aggregated and filtered by Open Targets rules; original studies may contain more detail
Datasets are large Parquet; only selected ones should be pulled
known_omissions: Rendered downloads page showed only 42 of the 61 datasets; the FTP listing is the complete inventory

reuse_decision.rationale: Already integrates GWAS credible sets, colocalisation, DepMap, CRISPR screens, IMPC, ClinGen, ClinVar (EVA) and pharmacogenomics. Use it as the primary route for those dimensions instead of scraping each source; keep the originals only where Open Targets omits information.

Tissue and cell-type expression; GTEx median TPM is already acquired directly.

sources.name: PDBe SIFTS: PDB chain to UniProt residue mappings

version.value: SIFTS flat files of 2026-10-18 (PDB release 42.26, UniProt 2026.03 per the file header); overwritten at each weekly PDB release

sources.scope: Residue-level mapping between experimentally determined PDB chains and UniProtKB sequences: mapped segments of each chain, and the segments whose residues are observed in the structure.
sources.mapping_methods: SIFTS pipeline: sequence alignment of each PDB chain to UniProtKB, giving contiguous segments in SEQRES, PDB-author and UniProt numbering.

quantitative.summary: Residue ranges of mapped and of observed segments.

licence.name: EMBL-EBI Terms of Use: freely available, no additional restriction on contributed data beyond the data owner's terms (terms page, verified live). PDB archive data files are CC0 1.0 (wwPDB usage policy, verified live). No SIFTS-specific licence statement was found.
licence.redistribution: Free with attribution; the SIFTS page asks users to cite Dana, Gutmanas et al., Nucleic Acids Research 47, D482 (2019).

coverage_limitations: Only experimentally determined structures; predicted models are in AlphaFold DB
A mapped segment says which UniProt residues a chain covers, not whether the construct carries engineered changes, nor the quality of the structure
Residue numbering differs between the SEQRES, PDB-author and UniProt systems; the UniProt columns are the ones used here
known_omissions: The other SIFTS flat files in the same directory (Pfam, InterPro, GO, CATH, SCOP, Ensembl, taxonomy, enzyme, PubMed) and the per-entry XML files are not fetched; InterPro and GO are held through InterPro and Open Targets
Coordinate files of the structures are not fetched

reuse_decision.rationale: Experimental-structure coverage per UniProt residue is the complement to the AlphaFold DB predicted models and was an explicit gap in the library (PDB not catalogued). The two summary files are small (6.3 MB and 11.0 MB). Structure coordinate files are not mirrored.

status.notes: Flat files listed with dates in the FTP index; the files are replaced each week, so the manifest records the size and SHA-256 of the copy fetched on 2026-10-25. pdb_chain_uniprot.tsv.gz uses CRLF line endings (a parser that splits on LF alone keeps a trailing carriage return in the last column); uniprot_segments_observed.tsv.gz uses LF.

sources.name: PharmVar (Pharmacogene Variation Consortium)

version.value: PharmVar 6.2.29 (site footer "Last Updated Sep 22 2026"; VCF fileDate 2026-09-22), the latest version listed on 2026-10-25

sources.scope: Haplotype (star allele) definitions of 15 pharmacogenes (CYP1A2, CYP2A13, CYP2A6, CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP3A4, CYP3A5, CYP4F2, DPYD, NAT2, NUDT15, SLCO1B1) in the complete-database download: a table of defining variants per haplotype and a VCF per haplotype on RefSeqGene, GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates, plus haplotype FASTA. API services are offered for third parties.
sources.mapping_methods: Positions given on locus reference sequences (RefSeqGene/LRG) and genome builds.

quantitative.summary: Haplotype definitions, not effect sizes.

licence.name: CC BY-SA 4.0 for the PharmVar database content, with the user agreeing to use the data for research purposes and not to offer any part of it for sale as a commercial item; access is under the site's Terms and Conditions (last modified 2023-03-24, which also contain an arbitration clause). Verified live at /terms-and-conditions.
licence.redistribution: Share-alike with attribution: adaptations must be shared under CC BY-SA 4.0 and no part of the data may be offered for sale as a commercial item. Contributed content is CC BY 4.0. The data here stay in git-ignored data/external/.

coverage_limitations: Haplotypes defined by structural variation are not included in downloads (per the download page)
Downloads are not available for transcript reference sequences
known_omissions: Other pharmacogenes in PharmVar that are not part of the complete-database download (for example genes still under review)
CPIC/ClinPGx allele function and phenotype assignments are separate sources (cpic, pharmgkb)

reuse_decision.rationale: The licence was readable after all (the earlier guessed URLs returned the application shell; the terms are linked from the footer of the rendered page), it permits research use with attribution and share-alike, and the complete database is one 193 MB archive that the site's own button serves. It closes the star-allele sequence gap that CPIC and ClinPGx tables leave.

status.notes: Terms at /terms-and-conditions (footer link). The Download Complete Database button calls get-download-file?name=ALL&refSeq=ALL&fileType=zip&version=current; the same URL with version=6.2.29 returns a byte-identical archive (SHA-256 compared) and is the pinned target.

sources.name: UniProtKB (Swiss-Prot and TrEMBL)

version.value: Release 2026_03 (150,006,383 entries; Swiss-Prot 575,748)

sources.scope: Protein sequences with curated function, domains, variants, PTMs and cross-references. 20,431 reviewed (Swiss-Prot) human entries. The humsavar variant index (release 2026_03, 02-Sep-2026) lists 85,015 rows for 83,859 distinct Swiss-Prot human missense variants (rows 33,333 LP/P, 39,964 LB/B, 11,718 US; a variant with several diseases has one row per disease) with ACMG/AMP-style categories curated from the literature.
formats: flat files and FASTA on FTP
sources.mapping_methods: Cross-references to Ensembl, RefSeq, HGNC, PDB and AlphaFold DB.

licence.redistribution: Attribution

coverage_limitations: Curated annotation lags primary literature
Variant sections are not systematic experimental measurements
humsavar categories are literature-curated, for research use only (stated in the file) and may change; protein-level only (UniProt canonical numbering), no genomic coordinates

reuse_decision.rationale: Primary source; fetch the reviewed human table with identifier cross-references (needed to join protein-level MaveDB targets to genes and structures) and the humsavar missense variant index (a protein-level clinical annotation that joins to MaveDB variants through UniProt accession and amino-acid change).
